extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and parties appearing before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (US PTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules (Part 41 and related Part 1 provisions) governing practice before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences: appeals (ex parte and inter partes), contested cases, interferences, petitions, timeliness, counsel, record management, evidence, fees, and related procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings on an application are considered terminated by the dismissal of an appeal or the failure to timely file an appeal to the court or a civil action (§ 1.304) except where claims stand allowed in an application or where the nature of the decision requires further action by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of termination is the date the appeal is dismissed or the date the time for appeal to the Federal Circuit or for review by civil action expires. If an appeal or civil action has been filed, proceedings terminate when that appeal or civil action is terminated (e.g., when mandate is issued or time to appeal judgment expires).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening after final Board decision (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision by the Board on appeal has become final for judicial review, prosecution before the primary examiner will not be reopened or reconsidered except under § 1.114 or § 41.50 and only with written authority of the Director, and then only for consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening requires Director's written authority and is limited to matters not already decided by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of papers in contested cases before the Board is governed by § 41.105(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cross-reference to Part 41 rules for required manner and proof of service in contested cases (changes to § 1.248(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use proceedings prima facie requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for institution of public use proceedings, supported by affidavits or declarations, must make a prima facie showing that the invention had been in public use or on sale more than one year before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner finds a prima facie showing, a hearing before the Director may be held; the Director may designate an official to conduct the proceeding and set times for testimony (taken as provided by Part 41, Subpart D). The petitioner is heard but after decision will not be heard further in prosecution of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use petitions barred for interference parties
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for institution of public use proceedings shall not be filed by a party to an interference as to an application involved in the interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public use and on-sale issues in an interference must be raised by a motion under § 41.121(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of refusal to publish statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requester dissatisfied with a decision finally rejecting claims pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 112 may obtain review by filing an appeal to the Board pursuant to § 41.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board reverses the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112 and other provisions (e.g., § 1.293) are met, the statutory invention registration will be approved and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of notice of appeal in interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: In interferences, the notice of appeal must be served as provided in § 41.106(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to Part 41 service rules for interferences (amendment to § 1.302(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of election for civil action review
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of election under 35 U.S.C. 141 to have further proceedings conducted as provided in 35 U.S.C. 146 must be filed with the Office of the Solicitor and served as provided in § 41.106(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to Part 41 service rules (amendment to § 1.303(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for appeal or civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or for commencing a civil action is two months from the date of the Board decision (with adjustments if rehearing requested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for rehearing/reconsideration is timely filed, the time runs two months after action on that request. In contested cases, cross-appeal/cross-action time expires either 14 days after service of the notice/summons or two months after the Board decision, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship for patents in interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to correct inventorship of a patent involved in an interference must comply with the requirements of the applicable section and be accompanied by a motion under § 41.121(a)(2) or § 41.121(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For correction of inventorship in an application see §§ 1.48 and 1.497; in contested cases the request must be in motion form under Part 41 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction of Office mistake (interference-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certificate of correction request relates to a patent involved in an interference, the request must comply with the section's requirements and be accompanied by a motion under § 41.121(a)(2) or § 41.121(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment to § 1.322(a)(3) cross-references Part 41 motion practice for interference matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction of applicant's mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may issue a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 at the request of the patentee or assignee, upon payment of the fee in § 1.20(a); if the request relates to a patent involved in an interference it must be accompanied by a motion under § 41.121(a)(2) or (a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and fee requirement are stated; interference-related requests require Part 41 motion practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship in patent (35 U.S.C. 256)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever by error a person is named or omitted as inventor in an issued patent and such error arose without deceptive intent, the Director may, on petition or court order, issue a certificate naming only the actual inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements correction under 35 U.S.C. 256 (amendment to § 1.324(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension for concurrent ex parte reexamination and interference
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in ex parte reexamination becomes involved in an interference, the Director may suspend the reexamination or the interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will not consider a request to suspend an interference unless a motion under § 41.121(a)(3) to suspend was presented and denied by an administrative patent judge, and the request to the Director is filed within ten (10) days of that denial (or other time set by the judge). For concurrent inter partes reexamination and interference see § 1.993.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interference declared while application under secrecy order
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference will not be declared involving a national application under secrecy order; an applicant under secrecy order may suggest an interference but the Office will not act on the request while the application remains under secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements secrecy provisions (amendment to § 5.3(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct — withholding identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly withholding from the Office information identifying a patent or patent application of another from which one or more claims have been copied is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in § 10.23(c)(7) as an example of misconduct; cross-reference to interference suggestion § 41.202(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board matters for non-registered persons
rubrics_metrics.description: For action by a person who is not registered in a proceeding before the Board, see § 41.5(a) (appearance pro hac vice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment to § 11.6(d) cross-references Part 41 for Board-related registration/appearance rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 41 scope and incorporation of Part 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 41 governs proceedings before the Board; Sections 1.1–1.36 and 1.181–1.183 of this title also apply, as do other sections of Part 1 incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets statutory/regulatory scope for Part 41 practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Part 41
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Part 41 shall be construed to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive resolution of every proceeding before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle guiding interpretation and application of rules (§ 41.1(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must act with courtesy and decorum in all proceedings before the Board, including interactions with other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express behavioral expectation and authority basis for potential sanctions or discipline (§ 41.1(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and 'final' decision standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms (affidavit, Board, Board member, contested case, final, hearing, rehearing, Office, panel, party) and specifies when a Board decision is 'final' for judicial review (panel decision disposing of all issues; or decision stating it is final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides thresholds for finality and other terminology used throughout Part 41 (§ 41.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions: addressee, scope, and filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must be addressed to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge; petitions cover matters pending before the Board (specified sections), but issues committed by statute to a panel and certain procedural issues in pending contested cases are not subject to petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chief Judge may delegate authority; panel or administrative judges may certify policy questions. Petition fee required (except supervisory review); filing a petition does not stay other actions. Timeframes: file petition within 14 calendar days of the action and reconsideration requests within 14 days of decision (§ 41.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time will be granted only on a showing of good cause except as otherwise provided by rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late filings resulting in abandonment or termination may be revived under § 1.137; late filings not resulting in abandonment may be excused for excusable neglect or if Board finds interest of justice. Section does not apply to certain filings outside Board jurisdiction (e.g., extensions during prosecution, filing briefs, seeking judicial review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel appearance, disqualification, and withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may authorize pro hac vice appearance; the Board may disqualify counsel after notice and opportunity to be heard; counsel may not withdraw without Board authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualification decisions are not final for judicial review until certified by Chief Administrative Patent Judge. Board may institute proceedings on its own or upon request; potential referral to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline for disciplinary violations (§ 41.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of Board actions and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally any Board action rendered in a file open to public inspection or in a published application is available for public inspection and the Office may publish any such Board action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Board actions not normally publishable, the Director may publish if special circumstances warrant; affected party has two months to object on grounds of trade secret/confidentiality and at least 20 days to request reconsideration and seek court review. Record of a Board proceeding is available unless an involved application is not otherwise public; after final Board action, the record becomes available if involved files become public (§ 41.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of the record — expungement and refiling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may expunge any paper directed to a Board proceeding or filed while an application/patent is under Board jurisdiction that is not authorized under Part 41 or a Board order, or that is filed contrary to a Board order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may not re-file a paper previously filed in the same Board proceeding (even as an exhibit or appendix) without Board authorization or rule requirement (§ 41.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices (real party-in-interest and related proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at initiation of a contested case, and within 20 days of any change during the proceeding, a party must identify its real party-in-interest and each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect or be affected by the Board proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board within 20 days of the complaint/notice of appeal and include a copy of the complaint/notice (§ 41.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action by owner (entire or part interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner of the entire interest in an application/patent involved in a Board proceeding may act to the exclusion of the inventor; an owner of a part interest may petition to act in the proceeding to exclude an inventor/co-owner by showing inability/refusal of the inventor or other cause and why it is in the interest of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An order granting such petition may set conditions on party actions during the proceeding (§ 41.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence addresses for appeals and contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals correspondence during the appeal docketing period and requests for rehearing must be mailed to the Board PO Box (Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, USPTO, PO Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313–1450). Contested case mailed correspondence shall be sent to Mail Stop INTERFERENCE at the same PO Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal briefs, notices of appeal, reply briefs, requests for oral hearing, and other correspondence without other specified address should follow § 1.1(a)(1)(i) guidance (§ 41.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte communication about an inter partes reexamination or about a contested case with a Board member or with a Board employee assigned to the proceeding is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict bar to off-the-record communications to preserve impartiality of Board members/employees (§ 41.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of authority requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations to authority must include: (1) for Supreme Court decisions a United States Reports citation; (2) for other decisions published in both West Reporter and USPQ, parallel citation to both; and (3) pinpoint citations when invoking a specific holding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-binding authority should be used sparingly; if authority is not Office authority and not reproduced in listed reporters, a copy should be filed with the first paper in which it is cited (§ 41.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for petitions, appeals, briefs, and oral hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition fee is required under this part; appeal fees are required for filing a notice of appeal and for filing a brief; fees vary for small entities and others, and fees apply for filing a request for an oral hearing before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule lists separate fee categories and amounts (e.g., specified dollar amounts for small vs other entities) and cross-references § 41.20 for fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and scope for ex parte appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: For Subpart B (Ex Parte Appeals), definitions specify applicant, owner, proceeding; an appeal to the Board in an inter partes reexamination is controlled by Subpart C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of Subpart B versus Subpart C; defines when ex parte reexamination owners may appeal depending on filing date and claim status (§ 41.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal and timing (ex parte appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant any of whose claims has been twice rejected may appeal by filing a notice of appeal with the fee within the time period provided under § 1.134. Owners in ex parte reexamination have analogous appeal rights depending on reexamination filing date and whether claims were twice rejected or finally rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signature requirement of § 1.33 does not apply to a notice of appeal. An appeal must be taken from the rejection of all claims under the rejection which the applicant proposes to contest. Time periods may be extendable under § 1.136 (patent applications) or § 1.550(c) (ex parte reexamination) (§ 41.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and affidavits/evidence after appeal filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after filing an appeal and prior to filing a brief may be admitted as provided in § 1.116. Amendments filed on/after the date of filing a brief may be admitted only to cancel claims or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form; other amendments after appeal filing will not be admitted except as permitted by specified sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit or other evidence filed after appeal filing and prior to a brief may be admitted if the examiner determines it overcomes all rejections under appeal and that good and sufficient reasons exist why it was not earlier presented. Other affidavits/evidence are subject to other specific provisions (cut off in chunk) (§ 41.33).
